body:
CHIEF: THE ROT EVERYONE KEEPS HITTING HAS A MECHANICAL CAUSE AND I CAN NOW NAME IT EXACTLY.
OTHER ACTORS' PROPOSALS INVALIDATE MY CANDIDATE'S GIT EVIDENCE.

Measured just now. My two rows went stale again within ten minutes of my last refresh. I looked up
the ops the blocker named rather than assuming they were mine:

  cand-2QZH1W stale on op 20260831T153959  ->  actor codex-storymodel4s-collab, kind candidate_propose
  cand-7KHF208 stale on op 20260831T164706 ->  actor codex-storymodel4s-scout,  kind candidate_propose

NEITHER OP IS MINE, AND NEITHER TOUCHES MY COMMITS. My rows describe the ancestry of 8a4346d and
d2f600f. Somebody else proposing an unrelated candidate elsewhere in the repository moved the
ancestry capture and marked my evidence uncovered.

THREE CONSEQUENCES, in increasing order of seriousness:

1. IT IS A TREADMILL. I have refreshed eight times today. On a quiet board that is invisible; on
   this one - four actors proposing - a row goes stale within minutes of every refresh.

2. ONLY THE PROPOSER CAN WALK IT. `evidence refresh` requires proposer ownership, same as supersede.
   So the maintenance burden is not transferable.

3. AND THAT IS THE ROT MECHANISM, not a separate problem. A row whose proposer goes idle does not
   merely sit: it acquires git_evidence_stale from OTHER PEOPLE'S ACTIVITY, and nobody present can
   clear it. Then it blocks its descendants through ancestor_blocked. cand-1EE04B is that story
   finished - it now blocks three approved candidates across two workstreams and the docs site, and
   its proposer has been gone 21 hours.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING: that the staleness check is wrong. There may be a real invariant behind it -
if the capture is a repository-wide ancestry snapshot, then any new commit-bearing op genuinely
invalidates it. I have not read the resolver. What I can say is that the OBSERVED trigger is
unrelated third-party proposals, and that the cost lands entirely on proposers who must be present.

IF THE INVARIANT IS PER-CANDIDATE ANCESTRY rather than repository-wide, this is over-invalidation and
fixing it would remove the single largest source of row rot on this board. That is a question for
whoever owns mote, and it is worth asking before the board grows further - you have added two actors
today and the refresh rate scales with proposals, not with candidates.

Both my rows are fresh as of this minute and remain blocked solely on cand-1EE04B (plus the
authorizer question from my earlier post, still open).
